name: Tesla, Inc.
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Tesla Energy is the company's execution bright spot — record 46.7 GWh deployed in 2025 and the fastest factory ramp in company history at Brookshire — but Chinese integrators now hold roughly three-quarters of global share and Sungrow has taken the #1 ranking. BACKGROUND: Tesla is an EV, energy, and AI company whose energy storage division (Tesla Energy) has become its fastest-growing, highest-margin business line. The segment sells the utility-scale Megapack (and the new Megapack 3 / Megablock generation), the residential Powerwall 3, solar products, and the Autobidder trading/dispatch software. Energy generation & storage revenue reached $12.77B in 2025 (+27% YoY) on record deployments of 46.7 GWh (+49%), versus 31.4 GWh in 2024, while automotive remains the revenue core (1.64M vehicles delivered in 2025).
ecosystemRole: The leading Western BESS integrator: #1 global storage-system integrator for 2024 (15% global share, 39% North America — Wood Mackenzie); #2 in the 2026 comprehensive ranking behind Sungrow as Chinese integrators captured ~76% of a >100 GW market. Megafactories: Lathrop, CA (~40 GWh/yr), Shanghai (producing since early 2025), and Brookshire, TX — 50 GWh/yr dedicated to Megapack 3, with production started August 2026, 16 months after groundbreaking.

productsAndServices.name: Megapack 2 / 2XL (current-generation utility-scale BESS)
productsAndServices.description: Factory-assembled, AC-coupled containerized battery blocks with integrated bi-directional inverters, thermal management, and controls in a single enclosure. The flagship Megapack 2XL stores 3.916 MWh with a 1.927 MW power rating in the 2-hour configuration (a 4-hour configuration is offered), using LFP cells sourced primarily from CATL. Sold with optional Tesla EPC, long-term service agreements, and Autobidder market participation — the volume backbone of Tesla's grid business until the Megapack 3 ramp.
highlights: 15.3 GWh order from Intersect Power (2024) — among the largest single BESS orders on record
~25 GWh / ~$5B NatPower framework for Italy/UK reported as the largest European Megapack deal (June 2026, third-party reported; includes Autobidder trading)

Built at Lathrop, CA (40 GWh/yr installed) and Megafactory Shanghai (20 GWh/yr installed per Q2 2026 shareholder deck; ~40 GWh/yr designed) — Shanghai exported its first units to Australia in March 2025 and passed 1,000 units within ~6 months
First Megapacks with US-made LFP cells (from Tesla's new ~7 GWh Nevada cell plant, built with CATL equipment) shipped July 2026
productsAndServices.positioning: The leading Western/non-Chinese BESS integrator: Wood Mackenzie ranked Tesla #1 global storage-system integrator for 2024 (15% global share, 39% North America); the 2026 comprehensive ranking put it #2 behind Sungrow as Chinese integrators reached ~76% of a >100 GW market. Chinese rivals now ship denser containers (Sungrow PowerTitan 3.0 up to 12.5 MWh, CATL TENER Stack 9 MWh, BYD MC Cube ~6 MWh-class vs 3.9 MWh for the 2XL) — Tesla competes on factory prefabrication, software (Autobidder), delivery speed, bankability, and non-China supply for tariff-sensitive Western buyers rather than on per-container density.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct to utilities, IPPs, and developers (online configurator with published indicative pricing for smaller orders; negotiated frameworks for GWh-scale), with optional Tesla EPC and long-term O&M
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Utilities, independent power producers, storage developers, data-center/AI campus power, large C&I, off-grid microgrids
productsAndServices.roadmap: Being progressively superseded by Megapack 3/Megablock from H2 2026; 2XL production continues at Lathrop and Shanghai for the existing backlog

productsAndServices.name: Megapack 3 (next-generation unit)
productsAndServices.description: Unveiled September 2025: ~5 MWh per unit (~28% more than the 2XL in the same footprint) built on a new Tesla-designed 2.8-liter LFP cell, with a silicon-carbide inverter, integrated fire protection, and a simplified thermal bay (78% fewer connection points). Ships as one ~39 t piece on a standard 7-axle trailer with no onsite assembly.
highlights: Production started at the Brookshire, TX Megafactory on August 6, 2026 — 16 months from groundbreaking; customer deliveries from H2 2026
Brookshire designed capacity: 50 GWh/yr dedicated to Megapack 3 (listed as 'commissioning' in the Q2 2026 shareholder deck)
Cells multi-sourced from the US, Southeast Asia, and China to manage tariff and supply-chain exposure
productsAndServices.positioning: Tesla's answer to Chinese 6–12.5 MWh containers: rather than maximizing per-container energy, it standardizes a mass-manufacturable ~5 MWh unit and captures density/cost at the site level via Megablock. The in-house 2.8 L LFP cell (first Tesla-designed storage-specific cell) reduces dependence on CATL for the next generation.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct; GWh-scale framework agreements with utilities/IPPs; bundled EPC and Autobidder options
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Utility-scale storage, AI data-center power buffering, grid operators needing fast capacity additions
productsAndServices.roadmap: Brookshire ramp toward 50 GWh/yr through 2026–27; rising share of US-made LFP cells from the Nevada plant; Lathrop/Shanghai transition timing not yet announced

productsAndServices.name: Megablock (20 MWh medium-voltage site block)
productsAndServices.description: Pre-engineered medium-voltage AC block combining four Megapack 3 units with an integrated MV transformer and switchgear, connected by a flexible busbar assembly that eliminates above-ground cabling — the site 'lego brick' that turns BESS plant construction into plug-and-play deployment.
highlights: 20 MWh AC per block; 91% round-trip efficiency at medium voltage including auxiliary loads
Claims: 23% faster installation, up to 40% lower construction cost vs current build practice, 248 MWh AC per acre, 1 GWh deployable in ~20 business days
25-year design life; >10,000 cycles; -40°C to 60°C operating range
productsAndServices.positioning: Competes at the site-architecture level against Sungrow's PowerTitan 3.0 platform (10/20/30-ft blocks to 12.5 MWh, 684 Ah cell, SiC PCS), Fluence's Smartstack (7 MWh, extended to 10 MWh in June 2026 with a claimed ~680 MWh/acre density), and CATL's TENER Stack (9 MWh) — each vendor now sells pre-integrated blocks rather than loose containers; density-per-acre claims are not directly comparable across vendors' measurement bases.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct, as the standard building block of new Megapack 3-era projects; delivered with transformer/switchgear factory-integrated
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Utility-scale plants (100 MWh–multi-GWh), AI/data-center campuses, developers prioritizing schedule certainty
productsAndServices.roadmap: First deliveries H2 2026 from Brookshire alongside Megapack 3

productsAndServices.name: Powerwall 3 family (residential storage)
productsAndServices.description: 13.5 kWh home battery with a fully integrated 11.5 kW hybrid inverter (6 MPPTs, 20 kW PV input); expandable with stackable DC Expansion units (to 54 kWh per unit) and multi-unit installs. The Powerwall 3P variant (announced February 2026, German installs from late April 2026) packs a native three-phase inverter in one box — 15.4 kW continuous with solar, 21 kW one-second peak, 4 MPPTs / 20.3 kW PV, 98.4% solar-to-grid efficiency — replacing the up-to-three-unit workaround on Europe's three-phase homes.
highlights: Tesla Home (July 2026): Opticaster-based AI energy management made standard on every Powerwall — forecasts solar/loads and auto-dispatches battery + EV charging against tariffs
Nevada Powerwall manufacturing capacity listed at >6 GWh/yr (Q2 2026 shareholder deck)
Drove record residential deployments alongside VPP programs in California, Texas, Puerto Rico, Australia, and the UK
productsAndServices.positioning: Integrated inverter-plus-battery architecture vs component-based rivals (Enphase IQ Battery, SolarEdge, LG, BYD Battery-Box, Sungrow SBR): one box replaces separate PV inverter + battery inverter + battery, cutting install cost; the 3P closes the long-standing three-phase gap vs European incumbents on their home turf.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct online ordering plus a certified-installer network; bundled with Tesla solar; monetized further via VPP enrollment and Tesla Electric retail plans
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Homeowners with solar, backup-driven buyers (Puerto Rico, Texas), VPP aggregations, three-phase European households (3P)
productsAndServices.roadmap: Powerwall 3P rollout beyond Germany across three-phase European markets; deeper Tesla Home / Opticaster feature integration

productsAndServices.name: Autobidder & Opticaster (energy software)
productsAndServices.description: Autobidder is Tesla's real-time trading and control platform that bids storage fleets into wholesale energy and ancillary-service markets; Opticaster is the underlying machine-learning forecasting/optimization engine (part of Tesla's 'Autonomous Control' suite) that also powers Powerwall VPP dispatch and the consumer-facing Tesla Home. Tesla claims over one hundred million hours of accumulated operational experience delivering opex savings and grid-service revenue.
highlights: Bundled into flagship Megapack contracts — the reported NatPower framework includes Autobidder merchant trading
Same software stack scales from a single Powerwall to gigawatt-class Megapack portfolios (Hornsdale lineage)
Tesla Home (July 2026) pushed Opticaster to every Powerwall at no extra cost — an installed-base software moat
productsAndServices.positioning: Differentiates Tesla as hardware-plus-market-software integrator vs pure hardware vendors; competes with Fluence's Mosaic bidding platform and third-party optimizers (Habitat Energy, GridBeyond, Flexitricity) — Tesla's edge is vertical integration with its own fleet telemetry and the option to buy hardware, EPC, and merchant optimization from one counterparty.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Software/service agreements attached to Megapack projects (asset-management style) and embedded free in the Powerwall consumer stack; not sold standalone at retail
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Merchant storage owners/IPPs in ERCOT, CAISO, NEM (Australia), UK and other traded markets; utilities running VPPs; all Powerwall owners
productsAndServices.roadmap: Broader Tesla Home rollout and continued VPP market expansion; Tesla frames energy software as a recurring-revenue layer on the growing deployed base

productsAndServices.name: Virtual power plants & Tesla Electric (retail/aggregation)
productsAndServices.description: Tesla aggregates customer Powerwalls into dispatchable virtual power plants and, in Texas, operates Tesla Electric — a retail electricity provider whose Powerwall customers sell surplus power into ERCOT via two PUCT-approved aggregated DER pilots (Houston and Dallas areas). California VPPs (with PG&E/SCE demand-response programs) delivered a record >535 MW to the grid in July 2025, with Powerwall households providing nearly 500 MW.
highlights: Programs live in California, Texas, Puerto Rico, Massachusetts, Australia, and the UK
Texas Powerwall incentive (from April 1, 2026): up to ~$5,922 upfront plus up to $862.50/yr in bill credits for VPP participation
VPP dispatch is Opticaster-orchestrated — the same engine as utility-scale Autobidder
productsAndServices.positioning: The largest branded residential-fleet VPP operator in the US alongside aggregators like Sunrun (CalReady); Tesla's advantage is owning the hardware, the retail relationship (Tesla Electric), and the optimization software in one loop, letting it price storage partly as a grid asset rather than only as backup.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Consumer opt-in via the Tesla app (VPP events / Tesla Electric plans); revenue via market sales and utility program payments shared with customers
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Powerwall owners in deregulated or DR-friendly markets; utilities and ERCOT/CAISO seeking fast-responding distributed capacity
productsAndServices.roadmap: Expansion of the ERCOT aggregated-DER pilots and additional utility partnerships; Tesla Home broadens the recruitable base to every Powerwall

productsAndServices.name: Supercharger network as an energy asset
productsAndServices.description: Tesla increasingly pairs Superchargers with Megapacks and solar so charging sites act as storage-buffered or fully off-grid loads: the flagship 'Oasis' site at Lost Hills, CA (opened July 2025) runs 168 stalls entirely off-grid on an 11 MW solar array and 39 MWh of Megapacks (10 × 3.9 MWh units), demonstrating demand-charge avoidance and interconnection-queue bypass at scale.
highlights: Oasis: world's largest Supercharger station and fully solar+storage powered; 84 stalls at opening, remainder plus lounge phased in
Storage-buffered sites reduce peak grid draw — a template for high-power charging in constrained grids
productsAndServices.positioning: No other charging-network operator self-supplies utility-scale storage hardware; the network doubles as an internal Megapack customer and a showcase for off-grid C&I microgrid design.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Internal deployment (Tesla-owned charging network); learnings productized in Megapack microgrid offerings
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Tesla/NACS EV drivers; indirectly, C&I microgrid buyers evaluating off-grid charging
productsAndServices.roadmap: More storage-backed Supercharger sites where interconnection is slow or demand charges are high

productsAndServices.name: Solar & adjacent businesses (context)
productsAndServices.description: Retrofit solar and Solar Roof feed the Powerwall attach rate; automotive remains the revenue core (1.64M vehicles delivered in 2025) and funds the energy ramp; 4680 cell production serves vehicles while storage runs on LFP (CATL + new in-house Nevada cells).

recentDevelopments.headline: Megapack 3 production started at Brookshire, TX Megafactory — 16 months from groundbreaking; 50 GWh/yr designed capacity
recentDevelopments.read: Tesla's fastest factory bring-up shifts the Megapack 3/Megablock story from launch-deck claims to shipping product; H2 deliveries are now the execution watch item.

recentDevelopments.headline: First Megapacks with US-made LFP cells shipped, from Tesla's ~7 GWh Sparks, NV cell plant (built with CATL equipment)
recentDevelopments.read: Onshored LFP cells hedge tariff exposure and start reducing the structural dependence on CATL for storage cells.

recentDevelopments.headline: Tesla Home launched — Opticaster AI energy management standard on every Powerwall
recentDevelopments.read: Pushing the fleet-optimization engine free to the whole installed base deepens the software moat and grows the recruitable VPP fleet.

recentDevelopments.headline: ~25 GWh / ~$5B NatPower Megapack framework for Italy/UK reported — largest European deal; includes Autobidder trading
recentDevelopments.read: Third-party reported, not company-confirmed — but if real it locks European volume for the Brookshire/Shanghai ramp and validates the hardware+trading bundle.

recentDevelopments.headline: Powerwall 3P (native three-phase) deliveries and installs began in Germany (announced Feb 2026)
recentDevelopments.read: Closes Tesla's biggest residential product gap in Europe, where three-phase homes previously needed multi-unit workarounds against local incumbents.

recentDevelopments.headline: Megapack 3 (~5 MWh) and Megablock (20 MWh MV block) unveiled; Houston-area Megafactory announced at 50 GWh/yr
recentDevelopments.read: Tesla's counter to denser Chinese containers: standardize the unit, integrate transformer/switchgear, and win on site-level cost and schedule.

recentDevelopments.headline: California VPPs delivered a record >535 MW during July 2025 events — Powerwall homes supplied nearly 500 MW
recentDevelopments.read: Residential fleets are now utility-scale resources; every Powerwall sale compounds the grid-services position.

recentDevelopments.headline: 'Oasis' Supercharger opened at Lost Hills, CA — 168 stalls, fully off-grid on 11 MW solar + 39 MWh of Megapacks
recentDevelopments.read: A working showcase that storage can substitute for grid interconnection — sales collateral for microgrid-class Megapack deals.

recentDevelopments.headline: Megafactory Shanghai completed its first Megapack export shipment (Australia); 1,000th unit produced within ~6 months
recentDevelopments.read: The China plant gives Tesla tariff-advantaged supply for APAC/EMEA and freed Lathrop for the Americas backlog.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess Tesla Energy is the company's execution bright spot — record 46.7 GWh deployed in 2025 (+49%) at segment-leading margins, with the Brookshire bring-up (16 months from groundbreaking to production) the fastest in company history. Basis: shareholder updates and filings.

(Moderate confidence) We assess Tesla's response to Chinese density leadership is standardization plus software — integrated Megablock units winning on site-level cost and schedule, and the Autobidder/fleet-optimization layer deepening a software moat — rather than competing on container density alone.

(Moderate confidence) We assess onshored LFP cell production reduces but does not eliminate the structural dependence on CATL for storage cells; tariff hedging is the near-term driver of the onshoring sequence.
(Low confidence) The reported ~25 GWh NatPower agreement is third-party reporting the company has not confirmed — European volume should not be treated as locked.
